source.text: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ὥστε ἐκβάλλειν αὐτὰ καὶ θεραπεύειν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having summoned the twelve disciples of him he gave to them authority over spirits unclean so as to cast out them and to heal every disease and every sickness.

en.L: And summoning {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them authority over unclean spirits, so as to cast them out and to heal every disease and every sickness.
en.B: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to drive them out, and to heal every disease and every illness.
en.R: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve followers together. He gave them power over evil spirits so that they could make the spirits leave people. He also gave them power to heal every kind of sickness and disease.

es.L: Y habiendo convocado a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce discípulos, les dio autoridad sobre espíritus impuros, de modo que los expulsaran y curaran toda enfermedad y todo mal.
es.B: Jesús llamó junto a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce discípulos y les dio autoridad sobre los espíritus impuros, para expulsarlos y para curar toda clase de enfermedades y dolencias.
es.R: Jesús reunió a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce seguidores. Les dio poder sobre los espíritus malignos, para que pudieran hacerlos salir de las personas. También les dio poder para sanar toda clase de enfermedades y dolencias.

fr.L: Et ayant appelé {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} douze disciples, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur donna autorité sur les esprits impurs, de manière à les chasser et à guérir toute maladie et toute infirmité.
fr.B: Jésus appela {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} douze disciples auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et leur donna autorité sur les esprits impurs, pour qu’ils les chassent et qu’ils guérissent toute maladie et toute infirmité.
fr.R: Jésus a réuni {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} douze disciples. Il leur a donné du pouvoir sur les esprits mauvais, pour qu’ils les fassent sortir des gens. Il leur a aussi donné le pouvoir de guérir toutes sortes de maladies.

sw.L: Na baada ya kuwaita wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili, aliwapa mamlaka juu ya pepo wachafu, ili kuwafukuza na kuponya kila ugonjwa na kila udhaifu.
sw.B: Yesu aliwaita {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili, akawapa mamlaka juu ya pepo wachafu, wawafukuze, na waponye kila aina ya ugonjwa na maradhi.
sw.R: Yesu aliwakusanya pamoja wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili. Aliwapa uwezo juu ya pepo wabaya, ili waweze kuwafukuza kutoka kwa watu. Pia aliwapa uwezo wa kuponya kila aina ya magonjwa na maradhi.

vi.L: Và gọi mười hai môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban cho họ thẩm quyền trên các linh ô uế, để đuổi chúng ra, và để chữa lành mọi thứ bệnh tật và mọi thứ đau yếu.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu gọi mười hai môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến và ban cho họ thẩm quyền trên các linh ô uế, để đuổi chúng ra, và để chữa lành mọi thứ bệnh tật, mọi thứ đau yếu.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu gọi mười hai môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại. Ngài ban cho họ quyền trên các tà linh, để họ đuổi các tà linh ra khỏi người ta. Ngài cũng ban cho họ quyền chữa lành mọi thứ bệnh tật.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 자기의 열두 제자를 불러 모으시고, 그들에게 더러운 영들을 [다스리는] 권한을 주셔서, 그것들을 쫓아내고 모든 질병과 모든 아픔을 고치게 하셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 열두 제자를 가까이 부르셔서, 더러운 영들을 다스리는 권한을 주셨다. 그들이 더러운 영들을 쫓아내고 온갖 질병과 온갖 아픔을 고치게 하신 것이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 열두 제자를 함께 부르셨다. 그리고 그들에게 악한 영들을 다스리는 권한을 주셨다. 그래서 그들이 사람들에게서 악한 영들을 쫓아낼 수 있게 하셨다. 또 온갖 병과 아픔을 고칠 수 있는 권한도 주셨다.

pt.L: E, chamando os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} doze discípulos, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes deu autoridade sobre espíritos impuros, para expulsá-los e para curar toda doença e toda enfermidade.
pt.B: Jesus chamou para junto de {{deity_pronoun:si|Si}} os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} doze discípulos e lhes deu autoridade sobre os espíritos impuros, para expulsá-los e para curar toda doença e toda enfermidade.
pt.R: Jesus reuniu os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} doze seguidores. Ele deu a eles poder sobre os espíritos maus, para que pudessem fazer esses espíritos saírem das pessoas. Também deu a eles poder para curar todo tipo de doença e enfermidade.

am.L: አሥራ ሁለቱን ደቀ መዛሙርቱንም ጠርቶ በርኩሳን መናፍስት ላይ ሥልጣን ሰጣቸው፤ ይህም እነርሱን እንዲያስወጡና ማንኛውንም በሽታና ማንኛውንም ሕመም እንዲፈውሱ ነው።
am.B: ኢየሱስ አሥራ ሁለቱን ደቀ መዛሙርቱን ወደ ራሱ ጠራ፤ ርኩሳን መናፍስትን የማስወጣትና ማንኛውንም በሽታና ሕመም የመፈወስ ሥልጣን ሰጣቸው።
am.R: ኢየሱስ አሥራ ሁለቱን ደቀ መዛሙርቱን በአንድነት ጠራ። ክፉ መናፍስትን ከሰዎች እንዲያስወጡ ኃይል ሰጣቸው። ማንኛውንም ዓይነት በሽታና ሕመም እንዲፈውሱም ኃይል ሰጣቸው።

ru.L: И, призвав своих двенадцать учеников, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} дал им власть над нечистыми духами, чтобы изгонять их и исцелять всякую болезнь и всякую немощь.
ru.B: Иисус подозвал к себе двенадцать учеников и дал им власть над нечистыми духами, чтобы они изгоняли их и исцеляли всякую болезнь и всякую немощь.
ru.R: Иисус собрал двенадцать учеников. Он дал им власть над нечистыми духами, чтобы они выгоняли этих духов из людей. А ещё {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} дал им силу исцелять все болезни и недуги.

hi.L: और अपने बारह चेलों को पास बुलाकर उन्होंने उन्हें अशुद्ध आत्माओं पर अधिकार दिया, कि उन्हें निकालें और हर प्रकार की बीमारी और हर प्रकार की दुर्बलता को दूर करें।
hi.B: यीशु ने अपने बारह चेलों को अपने पास बुलाया और उन्हें अशुद्ध आत्माओं पर अधिकार दिया, कि वे उन्हें निकालें और हर रोग और हर बीमारी को चंगा करें।
hi.R: यीशु ने अपने बारह चेलों को इकट्ठा किया। उन्होंने उन्हें बुरी आत्माओं पर अधिकार दिया, ताकि वे उन आत्माओं को लोगों में से निकाल सकें। उन्होंने उन्हें हर तरह की बीमारी और रोग को चंगा करने का अधिकार भी दिया।

uk.L: І, прикликавши дванадцятьох своїх учнів, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} дав їм владу над нечистими духами, щоб виганяти їх і зцілювати всяку хворобу й усяку неміч.
uk.B: Ісус покликав до себе дванадцятьох своїх учнів і дав їм владу над нечистими духами, щоб вони виганяли їх і зцілювали всяку хворобу й усяку неміч.
uk.R: Ісус зібрав дванадцятьох своїх учнів. Він дав їм владу над злими духами, щоб вони виганяли тих духів з людей. А ще дав їм силу зцілювати всякі хвороби й недуги.

ja.L: そして[イエスは]ご自分の十二人の弟子たちを呼び寄せて、汚れた霊たちに対する権威を彼らに授けられた。それらを追い出し、あらゆる病気とあらゆるわずらいを癒やすためである。
ja.B: イエスは十二人の弟子を呼び寄せ、汚れた霊に対する権威をお授けになった。汚れた霊を追い出し、あらゆる病気やわずらいを癒やすためである。
ja.R: イエスは十二人の弟子たちを呼び集められました。そして、汚れた霊を従わせる力を与えられました。人から汚れた霊を追い出すためです。また、どんな病気でも、体の弱さでも、いやす力を与えられました。

decisions.choice: authority over unclean spirits: the right and power to command them
decisions.reason: The genitive names what the authority is over. The next words say what it is for: to cast the spirits out.

decisions.choice: every disease and every sickness: the same words as 4:23 and 9:35
decisions.reason: Matthew describes the twelve's work in the words he used for Jesus's own work. They share in what he does.

decisions.choice: unclean spirits: demons
decisions.reason: Unclean spirits are the demons of 10:8. They are unclean because they are opposed to God and defile those they control.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: evil spirits
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer phrase for the same beings.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives (sus, sí, lo, mí)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("dio", "envió") and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("seguirme"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: espíritus impuros (L, B); espíritus malignos (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts. "Inmundo" is the traditional word but now sounds like dirt; "impuro" says the spirits make a person unfit to come near God, and Readable says plainly that they are evil, as the English does (meaning decision m3). "Toda enfermedad y todo mal" repeats the wording of 9:35 (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R)
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Gospels: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and taught. The long speech that follows (10:5-42) keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

decisions.choice: les esprits impurs (L, B), les esprits mauvais (R); disciples at every level
alternatives: les esprits impurs at Readable too
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:7: Readable uses a plainer phrase for the same beings, as the English Readable does. "Disciples" stays at Readable, where the English says "followers", as the style guide has it.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (wake, kwake, yangu)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Swahili carries most pronouns in the verb ("aliwapa", "alimsaliti"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John and Mark. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: pepo wachafu (L, B); pepo wabaya (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for unclean spirits, which are demons (meaning decision m3); Readable says plainly that they are evil, as the English does. "Kila ugonjwa na kila udhaifu" repeats the wording of 9:35 (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "linh ô uế" (L, B); "tà linh" (R) for unclean spirits
decisions.reason: The terms settled for the Gospels, as in Mark 6:7. Readable says "tà linh" (evil spirits), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "thẩm quyền" (L, B); "quyền" (R) for authority
decisions.reason: The word is the right and power to command (meaning decision); "thẩm quyền" names authority given to act, as in 9:6, and Readable uses the plain "quyền".

decisions.choice: "더러운 영" (L, B); "악한 영" (R); "권한" for authority; "열두 제자" where the Greek says "twelve disciples"
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 3:11 and 6:7: Literal and Balanced keep the word "unclean", Readable says "evil spirits", as the English Readable does. "권한" is authority given by someone. The words for disease and illness repeat the Korean of 4:23 and 9:35, as the Greek repeats its own (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 10; Jesus speaks to the twelve in 해라체
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so respect for Jesus is carried by -시-, 께서 and 그분 (docs/korean-style.md sections 4 and 7). The discourse of 10:5-42 is Jesus teaching his disciples, in the plain style.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus has nothing to change in Amharic; the pronouns (እርሱ, እሱ, the verb endings) are written once, with no span.

decisions.choice: ርኩሳን መናፍስት (L, B); ክፉ መናፍስት (R)
decisions.reason: ርኩስ መንፈስ (plural ርኩሳን መናፍስት) is the settled Amharic for an unclean spirit; Readable says ክፉ መናፍስት, 'evil spirits', as the English Readable does. ደቀ መዛሙርት stays at Readable too, where the English Readable says 'followers'.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; honorific third person for Jesus (“उन्होंने”)
alternatives: a deity_pronoun span as in English
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus is carried by the honorific third person at every level.
“चेला” is the everyday Hindi word for a teacher's follower, so Readable keeps it.

decisions.choice: "нечистые духи" (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "unclean spirits"; Russian keeps "нечистые духи" at every level, as settled in Mark. "Злой" is kept for the Greek word for evil.

decisions.choice: "あらゆる病気とあらゆるわずらい" (L); "あらゆる病気やわずらい" (B); "どんな病気でも、体の弱さでも" (R), as in 9:35
decisions.reason: Matthew describes the twelve's work in the words he used for Jesus' own (m2), so each level repeats its wording from 9:35. Readable says "汚れた霊", the shared Gospel term, where the English Readable says evil spirits, and "力" for authority, as in Mark 6:7.

source.text: τῶν δὲ δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τὰ ὀνόματά ἐστιν ταῦτα· πρῶτος Σίμων ὁ λεγόμενος Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, Φίλιππος καὶ Βαρθολομαῖος, Θωμᾶς καὶ Μαθθαῖος ὁ τελώνης, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖος, Σίμων ὁ Καναναῖος καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης ὁ καὶ παραδοὺς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Of the and twelve apostles the names are these: first Simon the [one] called Peter and Andrew the brother of him, James the [son] of Zebedee and John the brother of him, \v 3 Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew the tax collector, James the [son] of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus, \v 4 Simon the Cananaean and Judas the Iscariot the [one] also having betrayed him.

en.L: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, the [one] called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the [son] of Zebedee, and John his brother; \v 3 Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the [son] of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus; \v 4 Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, the [one] who also betrayed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The twelve apostles were these. First came Simon, known as Peter, with his brother Andrew; then James son of Zebedee, with his brother John; \v 3 Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus; \v 4 Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, the man who betrayed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Here are the names of the twelve apostles. First was Simon, who was also called Peter. Then there was his brother Andrew. There were James and his brother John, the sons of Zebedee. \v 3 There were Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, and Matthew the tax collector. There were James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus. \v 4 And there were Simon the Zealot and Judas Iscariot. Judas was the one who later betrayed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y los nombres de los doce apóstoles son estos: primero, Simón, el llamado Pedro, y Andrés su hermano; Santiago el [hijo] de Zebedeo, y Juan su hermano; \v 3 Felipe y Bartolomé; Tomás y Mateo el publicano; Santiago el [hijo] de Alfeo, y Tadeo; \v 4 Simón el cananista, y Judas el Iscariote, el que también {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregó.
es.B: Estos son los nombres de los doce apóstoles. Primero, Simón, llamado Pedro, con su hermano Andrés; luego Santiago, hijo de Zebedeo, con su hermano Juan; \v 3 Felipe y Bartolomé; Tomás y Mateo, el cobrador de impuestos; Santiago, hijo de Alfeo, y Tadeo; \v 4 Simón el cananista y Judas Iscariote, el que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} traicionó.
es.R: Estos son los nombres de los doce apóstoles. El primero era Simón, al que también llamaban Pedro. Después estaba su hermano Andrés. Estaban Santiago y su hermano Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo. \v 3 Estaban Felipe, Bartolomé, Tomás y Mateo, el cobrador de impuestos. Estaban Santiago, hijo de Alfeo, y Tadeo. \v 4 Y estaban Simón el Zelote y Judas Iscariote. Judas fue el que más tarde {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} traicionó.

fr.L: Or les noms des douze apôtres sont ceux-ci : d’abord Simon, celui qu’on appelle Pierre, et André son frère ; Jacques, [le fils] de Zébédée, et Jean son frère ; \v 3 Philippe et Barthélemy ; Thomas et Matthieu le collecteur d’impôts ; Jacques, [le fils] d’Alphée, et Thaddée ; \v 4 Simon le Cananéen, et Judas Iscariot, celui-là même qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livra.
fr.B: Voici les noms des douze apôtres. D’abord Simon, qu’on appelle Pierre, avec son frère André ; puis Jacques, fils de Zébédée, avec son frère Jean ; \v 3 Philippe et Barthélemy ; Thomas, et Matthieu le collecteur d’impôts ; Jacques, fils d’Alphée, et Thaddée ; \v 4 Simon le Cananéen, et Judas Iscariot, l’homme qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trahit.
fr.R: Voici les noms des douze apôtres. Le premier était Simon, qu’on appelait aussi Pierre. Il y avait aussi son frère André. Il y avait Jacques et son frère Jean, les fils de Zébédée. \v 3 Il y avait Philippe, Barthélemy, Thomas, et Matthieu le collecteur d’impôts. Il y avait Jacques, le fils d’Alphée, et Thaddée. \v 4 Et il y avait Simon le Zélote et Judas Iscariot. C’est Judas qui, plus tard, {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a trahi.

sw.L: Basi majina ya mitume kumi na wawili ni haya: wa kwanza, Simoni, aitwaye Petro, na Andrea ndugu yake; Yakobo [mwana] wa Zebedayo, na Yohana ndugu yake; \v 3 Filipo na Bartholomayo; Tomaso na Mathayo mtoza ushuru; Yakobo [mwana] wa Alfayo, na Thadayo; \v 4 Simoni Mkananayo, na Yuda Iskariote, ambaye pia alimsaliti.
sw.B: Mitume kumi na wawili walikuwa hawa: wa kwanza Simoni, aliyeitwa Petro, pamoja na ndugu yake Andrea; kisha Yakobo mwana wa Zebedayo, pamoja na ndugu yake Yohana; \v 3 Filipo na Bartholomayo; Tomaso, na Mathayo mtoza ushuru; Yakobo mwana wa Alfayo, na Thadayo; \v 4 Simoni Mkananayo, na Yuda Iskariote, yule aliyemsaliti.
sw.R: Haya ndiyo majina ya wale mitume kumi na wawili. Wa kwanza alikuwa Simoni, ambaye pia aliitwa Petro. Kisha alikuwepo ndugu yake Andrea. Walikuwepo Yakobo na ndugu yake Yohana, wana wa Zebedayo. \v 3 Walikuwepo Filipo, Bartholomayo, Tomaso, na Mathayo mtoza ushuru. Walikuwepo Yakobo mwana wa Alfayo, na Thadayo. \v 4 Tena walikuwepo Simoni Mzelote na Yuda Iskariote. Yuda ndiye ambaye baadaye alimsaliti.

vi.L: Còn tên của mười hai sứ đồ là thế này: thứ nhất, Si-môn, người được gọi là Phi-e-rơ, và Anh-rê, anh em của ông; Gia-cơ, [con] của Xê-bê-đê, và Giăng, anh em của ông; \v 3 Phi-líp và Ba-thê-lê-my; Thô-ma và Ma-thi-ơ, người thu thuế; Gia-cơ, [con] của A-phê, và Tha-đê; \v 4 Si-môn người Ca-na-an, và Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt, là người cũng đã nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Đây là tên của mười hai sứ đồ: trước hết là Si-môn, cũng gọi là Phi-e-rơ, và Anh-rê, anh em của ông; Gia-cơ con Xê-bê-đê và Giăng, anh em của ông; \v 3 Phi-líp và Ba-thê-lê-my; Thô-ma và Ma-thi-ơ, người thu thuế; Gia-cơ con A-phê, và Tha-đê; \v 4 Si-môn người Ca-na-an, và Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt, người đã phản bội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đây là tên của mười hai sứ đồ. Người đầu tiên là Si-môn, cũng gọi là Phi-e-rơ. Rồi đến Anh-rê, anh em của Si-môn. Có hai anh em Gia-cơ và Giăng, con của Xê-bê-đê. \v 3 Có Phi-líp, Ba-thê-lê-my, Thô-ma, và Ma-thi-ơ, người thu thuế. Có Gia-cơ con của A-phê, và Tha-đê. \v 4 Còn có Si-môn, người được gọi là "người Nhiệt Thành", và Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt. Giu-đa là người về sau đã phản bội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 열두 사도의 이름은 이러하다. 첫째로 베드로라고 불리는 시몬과 그의 형제 안드레, 세베대의 [아들] 야고보와 그의 형제 요한, \v 3 빌립과 바돌로매, 도마와 세리 마태, 알패오의 [아들] 야고보와 다대오, \v 4 가나나인 시몬과 가룟 유다이다. [유다는] 그분을 넘겨준 사람이기도 하다.
ko.B: 열두 사도의 이름은 이렇다. 먼저 베드로라고 하는 시몬과 그의 형제 안드레, 세베대의 아들 야고보와 그의 형제 요한, \v 3 빌립과 바돌로매, 도마와 세리 마태, 알패오의 아들 야고보와 다대오, \v 4 가나나인 시몬, 그리고 가룟 유다이다. 유다는 예수를 배반한 사람이다.
ko.R: 열두 사도의 이름은 이렇다. 첫째는 시몬인데, 베드로라고도 불렸다. 그다음은 시몬의 형제 안드레였다. 세베대의 아들들인 야고보와 그의 형제 요한도 있었다. \v 3 빌립과 바돌로매와 도마와 세금을 걷던 마태도 있었다. 알패오의 아들 야고보와 다대오도 있었다. \v 4 그리고 열심당원 시몬과 가룟 유다가 있었다. 유다는 나중에 예수를 원수들에게 넘겨준 사람이다.

pt.L: Ora, os nomes dos doze apóstolos são estes: primeiro, Simão, o chamado Pedro, e André, o irmão dele; Tiago, o [filho] de Zebedeu, e João, o irmão dele; \v 3 Filipe e Bartolomeu; Tomé e Mateus, o cobrador de impostos; Tiago, o [filho] de Alfeu, e Tadeu; \v 4 Simão, o cananeu, e Judas Iscariotes, aquele que também {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} traiu.
pt.B: Os doze apóstolos eram estes: primeiro, Simão, conhecido como Pedro, e o seu irmão André; depois, Tiago, filho de Zebedeu, e o seu irmão João; \v 3 Filipe e Bartolomeu; Tomé e Mateus, o cobrador de impostos; Tiago, filho de Alfeu, e Tadeu; \v 4 Simão, o cananeu, e Judas Iscariotes, o homem que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} traiu.
pt.R: Estes são os nomes dos doze apóstolos. O primeiro era Simão, que também era chamado de Pedro. Depois vinha André, irmão dele. Havia Tiago e o seu irmão João, os filhos de Zebedeu. \v 3 Havia Filipe, Bartolomeu, Tomé e Mateus, o cobrador de impostos. Havia Tiago, filho de Alfeu, e Tadeu. \v 4 E havia Simão, o zelote, e Judas Iscariotes. Judas foi aquele que mais tarde {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} traiu.

am.L: የአሥራ ሁለቱ ሐዋርያት ስሞችም እነዚህ ናቸው፤ መጀመሪያ ጴጥሮስ የተባለው ስምዖን፣ ወንድሙ እንድርያስም፤ የዘብዴዎስ [ልጅ] ያዕቆብ፣ ወንድሙ ዮሐንስም፤ \v 3 ፊልጶስና በርተሎሜዎስ፤ ቶማስና ቀራጩ ማቴዎስ፤ የእልፍዮስ [ልጅ] ያዕቆብና ታዴዎስ፤ \v 4 ቀነናዊው ስምዖንና እርሱን አሳልፎ የሰጠውም የአስቆሮቱ ይሁዳ።
am.B: የአሥራ ሁለቱ ሐዋርያት ስሞች እነዚህ ናቸው፤ በመጀመሪያ ጴጥሮስ የሚባለው ስምዖንና ወንድሙ እንድርያስ፤ ከዚያም የዘብዴዎስ ልጅ ያዕቆብና ወንድሙ ዮሐንስ፤ \v 3 ፊልጶስና በርተሎሜዎስ፤ ቶማስና ቀራጩ ማቴዎስ፤ የእልፍዮስ ልጅ ያዕቆብና ታዴዎስ፤ \v 4 ቀነናዊው ስምዖንና እርሱን አሳልፎ የሰጠው የአስቆሮቱ ይሁዳ።
am.R: የአሥራ ሁለቱ ሐዋርያት ስሞች እነዚህ ናቸው። የመጀመሪያው ጴጥሮስ ተብሎም የሚጠራው ስምዖን ነበር። ከዚያም ወንድሙ እንድርያስ ነበረ። የዘብዴዎስ ልጆች ያዕቆብና ወንድሙ ዮሐንስም ነበሩ። \v 3 ፊልጶስ፣ በርተሎሜዎስ፣ ቶማስና ቀራጩ ማቴዎስም ነበሩ። የእልፍዮስ ልጅ ያዕቆብና ታዴዎስም ነበሩ። \v 4 ቀናተኛው ስምዖንና የአስቆሮቱ ይሁዳም ነበሩ። ይሁዳ በኋላ ኢየሱስን አሳልፎ የሰጠው ነው።

ru.L: Имена же двенадцати апостолов таковы: первый — Симон, называемый Петром, и Андрей, брат его; Иаков Зеведеев и Иоанн, брат его; \v 3 Филипп и Варфоломей; Фома и Матфей мытарь; Иаков Алфеев и Фаддей; \v 4 Симон Кананит и Иуда Искариот, который и предал {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}.
ru.B: Вот двенадцать апостолов. Первым был Симон, называемый Петром, и его брат Андрей; затем Иаков, сын Зеведея, и его брат Иоанн; \v 3 Филипп и Варфоломей; Фома и Матфей, сборщик налогов; Иаков, сын Алфея, и Фаддей; \v 4 Симон Кананит и Иуда Искариот, тот, кто предал {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}.
ru.R: Вот имена двенадцати апостолов. Первым был Симон, которого называли ещё Петром. Потом его брат Андрей. Потом Иаков и его брат Иоанн, сыновья Зеведея. \v 3 Ещё были Филипп, Варфоломей, Фома и Матфей, сборщик налогов. Были Иаков, сын Алфея, и Фаддей. \v 4 И ещё Симон Зилот и Иуда Искариот. Иуда — это тот, кто потом предал {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}.

hi.L: और बारह प्रेरितों के नाम ये हैं: पहला शमौन, जो पतरस कहलाता है, और उसका भाई अन्द्रियास; जब्दी का [पुत्र] याकूब, और उसका भाई यूहन्ना; \v 3 फिलिप्पुस और बरतुल्मै; थोमा और महसूल लेनेवाला मत्ती; हलफई का [पुत्र] याकूब, और तद्दै; \v 4 शमौन कनानी, और यहूदा इस्करियोती, जिसने उन्हें पकड़वा भी दिया।
hi.B: बारह प्रेरितों के नाम ये थे। सबसे पहले शमौन, जो पतरस कहलाता है, और उसका भाई अन्द्रियास; फिर जब्दी का पुत्र याकूब और उसका भाई यूहन्ना; \v 3 फिलिप्पुस और बरतुल्मै; थोमा, और कर वसूलनेवाला मत्ती; हलफई का पुत्र याकूब, और तद्दै; \v 4 शमौन कनानी, और यहूदा इस्करियोती, वही जिसने उन्हें पकड़वाया।
hi.R: बारह प्रेरितों के नाम ये हैं। पहला शमौन था, जिसे पतरस भी कहते थे। फिर उसका भाई अन्द्रियास था। फिर जब्दी का बेटा याकूब और उसका भाई यूहन्ना थे। \v 3 फिर फिलिप्पुस, बरतुल्मै, थोमा, और कर वसूलनेवाला मत्ती थे। फिर हलफई का बेटा याकूब, और तद्दै थे। \v 4 और शमौन जेलोतेस और यहूदा इस्करियोती थे। यहूदा वही था जिसने बाद में यीशु को पकड़वा दिया।

uk.L: Імена ж дванадцятьох апостолів ось які: перший Симон, якого називають Петром, і Андрій, його брат; Яків Зеведеїв та Іван, його брат; \v 3 Филип і Варфоломій; Хома й Матвій митар; Яків Алфеїв і Тадей; \v 4 Симон Кананіт і Юда Іскаріот, який і видав {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}.
uk.B: Ось імена дванадцятьох апостолів. Першим був Симон, якого звуть Петром, з братом своїм Андрієм; далі Яків, син Зеведеїв, з братом своїм Іваном; \v 3 Филип і Варфоломій; Хома й Матвій, збирач податків; Яків, син Алфеїв, і Тадей; \v 4 Симон Кананіт і Юда Іскаріот, той, що видав {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}.
uk.R: Ось імена дванадцятьох апостолів. Першим був Симон, якого ще називали Петром. Потім його брат Андрій. Були там Яків та його брат Іван, сини Зеведея. \v 3 Були Филип, Варфоломій, Хома й Матвій, збирач податків. Були Яків, син Алфея, і Тадей. \v 4 І були Симон Зилот та Юда Іскаріот. Юда — це той, хто згодом зрадив {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}.

ja.L: さて、十二使徒の名は次のとおりである。まず、ペトロと呼ばれるシモンとその兄弟アンデレ、ゼベダイの[子]ヤコブとその兄弟ヨハネ、\v 3 フィリポとバルトロマイ、トマスと徴税人マタイ、アルファイの[子]ヤコブとタダイ、\v 4 熱心党のシモン、そしてイエスを引き渡した者、ユダ・イスカリオテである。
ja.B: 十二使徒の名は次のとおりである。まず、ペトロと呼ばれるシモンとその兄弟アンデレ、ゼベダイの子ヤコブとその兄弟ヨハネ、\v 3 フィリポとバルトロマイ、トマスと徴税人マタイ、アルファイの子ヤコブとタダイ、\v 4 熱心党のシモン、そしてイエスを裏切ったユダ・イスカリオテである。
ja.R: 十二人の使徒の名前は、次のとおりです。最初はシモンで、ペトロとも呼ばれていました。次に、その兄弟のアンデレがいました。それから、ゼベダイの子のヤコブと、その兄弟のヨハネがいました。\v 3 さらに、フィリポ、バルトロマイ、トマス、税金を集める人だったマタイ、アルファイの子ヤコブ、タダイがいました。\v 4 そして、熱心党のシモンと、ユダ・イスカリオテがいました。ユダは、後にイエスを敵に引き渡した人です。

decisions.choice: apostles: those sent out with authority to act for the one who sends them
decisions.reason: This is the only place Matthew uses the word. It comes from the verb "send out" used in 10:5 and 10:16.

decisions.choice: first: Peter heads the list
alternatives: the first one called, with no further sense
decisions.reason: Peter is named first in every list of the twelve (Mark 3:16; Luke 6:14; Acts 1:13), and he often speaks for them (16:16; 19:27).

decisions.choice: the Cananaean: from an Aramaic word meaning zealot, one zealous for God
decisions.reason: Luke 6:15 and Acts 1:13 call him "the Zealot". Whether this marks him as one who had fought against Roman rule or as one zealous for the law is not clear.

decisions.choice: Thaddaeus, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Lebbaeus, or Lebbaeus called Thaddaeus, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "Lebbaeus" here, and many later ones combine the two names. Luke 6:16 and Acts 1:13 name "Judas son of James" in this place in the list. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: betrayed: handed over to his enemies
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over. Matthew uses it for Judas giving Jesus up (26:15-16) and for the disciples' own arrest (10:17, 19, 21). The meaning of "Iscariot" is not certain; it may mean "man from Kerioth".

decisions.choice: Simon the Zealot (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the name as Matthew gives it; Readable gives its meaning, as Luke does.

decisions.choice: el cananista (L, B); el Zelote (R)
decisions.reason: The word comes from Aramaic and means a zealot (meaning decision m3, uncertain). Spanish "cananeo" means a Canaanite, a different people, so Literal and Balanced use the distinct form "cananista"; Readable gives the meaning, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: el publicano (L); el cobrador de impuestos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "publicano" is the traditional name for these tax farmers; Balanced and Readable say what Matthew's work was.

decisions.choice: le collecteur d’impôts
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 9) and Luke: "publicain" is a church word most readers no longer understand; "collecteur d’impôts" says what Matthew did.

decisions.choice: Simoni Mkananayo (L, B); Simoni Mzelote (R)
decisions.reason: The word comes from Aramaic and means a zealot (meaning decision m3, uncertain). "Mkanaani" would make him a Canaanite, a different people, so Literal and Balanced keep the form of the Greek name; Readable gives the meaning, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: mitume
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "mtume" is one sent out with authority to act for the one who sends him (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "sứ đồ" for apostles
decisions.reason: The Protestant word, settled with the tradition; "tông đồ" is the Catholic one. The apostles are those sent with authority to act for the one who sends them (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "anh em của ông" (L, B); "hai anh em" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 3:17 and 5:37: Vietnamese would have to say whether the brother is older or younger, which the Greek does not, so the neutral "anh em" is kept.

decisions.choice: "Si-môn người Ca-na-an" (L, B), "người Nhiệt Thành" (R); "nộp" (L), "phản bội" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Mark 3:18-19. The verb means handed over to his enemies (meaning decision): Literal keeps the word used through Matthew for handing over (10:17, 10:19, 10:21); Balanced and Readable say "betrayed", the usual word for Judas.

decisions.choice: "사도" at every level
decisions.reason: "사도" is the established Korean word, used in the Korean Mark 6:30; it means one sent with authority (meaning decision). Matthew uses the word only here.

decisions.choice: Protestant name forms as the Korean Mark 3:16-19; "가나나인 시몬" (L, B), "열심당원 시몬" (R); "넘겨준" (L, R), "배반한" (B); "세리" (L, B), "세금을 걷던" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 3:18-19, the parallel list: Readable gives the meaning of "Cananaean" (meaning decision) and says the plain thing about Judas and about Matthew's work.

decisions.choice: Simão, o cananeu (L, B); Simão, o zelote (R)
alternatives: Simão, o zelote at every level
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the name as Matthew gives it, as the English does; Readable gives its meaning (m3), as Luke does. "Cananeu" is the traditional Portuguese form, but it is also the word for a Canaanite ("a mulher cananeia", 15:22), which English "Cananaean" avoids; the meaning note and Readable's "zelote" guard against that reading. A reviewer may prefer "o zelote" at Balanced too.

decisions.choice: ቀነናዊው ስምዖን (L, B); ቀናተኛው ስምዖን (R)
decisions.reason: ቀነናዊ is the traditional Amharic form of the Greek title; Readable says what it means, ቀናተኛው, 'the zealous one', as the English Readable says 'the Zealot'. The two Amharic words happen to sound alike.

decisions.choice: “शमौन कनानी” (L, B); “शमौन जेलोतेस” (R)
decisions.reason: “कनानी” comes from the Aramaic for “zealot”, not from Canaan; Readable uses the name Luke gives him so readers are not misled.

decisions.choice: "Симон Кананит" (L, B); "Симон Зилот" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the name as Matthew gives it, in its traditional Russian form; Readable gives its meaning, the name Luke uses, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Симон Кананіт" (L, B); "Симон Зилот" (R)
decisions.reason: Kananaios comes from an Aramaic word for a zealot, not from Canaan; Literal and Balanced keep the Greek name, Readable gives its meaning, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "видав" (L, B); "зрадив" (R)
decisions.reason: Paradidōmi means to hand over; Literal and Balanced keep that sense, which links Judas with the handing over of the disciples in 10:17-21; Readable says what it was.

decisions.choice: "使徒" at every level
decisions.reason: The word names those sent out to act for the one who sends them (m1). "使徒" is the living Japanese word, and its kanji ("使", one sent) keep the link to the sending of 10:5 and 10:16.

decisions.choice: "熱心党のシモン" at every level
decisions.reason: The word comes from Aramaic for a zealot (m3). As in Mark 3:18, a transliteration would read in Japanese as a Canaanite, so the Gospels share "熱心党のシモン".

decisions.choice: "引き渡した" (L); "裏切った" (B); "敵に引き渡した" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over, and Matthew uses it also of the disciples' arrest (10:17, 19, 21; m5). Literal keeps the bare verb so the link shows; Balanced says betrayal, as in Mark 3:19.

source.text: Τούτους τοὺς δώδεκα ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς παραγγείλας αὐτοῖς λέγων· Εἰς ὁδὸν ἐθνῶν μὴ ἀπέλθητε καὶ εἰς πόλιν Σαμαριτῶν μὴ εἰσέλθητε·

records.literal_gloss: These the twelve sent out the Jesus having instructed them saying, Into a road of Gentiles not go off, and into a town of Samaritans not enter;

en.L: These twelve Jesus sent out, instructing them, saying, "Do not go off onto [the] road of [the] Gentiles, and do not enter a town of [the] Samaritans;
en.B: Jesus sent these twelve out, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} charged them: "Stay off the roads that lead to the Gentiles, and do not go into any Samaritan town.
en.R: Jesus sent out these twelve men. First {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them what to do: "Do not go to people who are not Jews. And do not go into any town where Samaritans live.

es.L: A estos doce los envió Jesús, mandándoles: «No {{plural_you:tomen|toméis}} [el] camino de [los] gentiles, ni {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en [ningún] pueblo de samaritanos;
es.B: Jesús envió a estos doce con estas órdenes: «No {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} por los caminos que llevan a los gentiles, ni {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en ningún pueblo samaritano.
es.R: Jesús envió a estos doce hombres. Primero les explicó lo que tenían que hacer: «No {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} adonde vive gente que no es judía. Y no {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en ningún pueblo donde vivan samaritanos.

fr.L: Ces douze, Jésus les envoya, après leur avoir donné des instructions, disant : « N’allez pas sur le chemin des nations, et n’entrez pas dans une ville de Samaritains ;
fr.B: Jésus envoya ces douze en mission avec ces consignes : « Ne prenez pas les routes qui mènent chez les non-Juifs, et n’entrez dans aucune ville samaritaine.
fr.R: Jésus a envoyé ces douze hommes en mission. D’abord, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a dit ce qu’ils devaient faire : « N’allez pas chez les gens qui ne sont pas juifs. Et n’entrez dans aucune ville où habitent des Samaritains.

sw.L: Hao kumi na wawili Yesu aliwatuma nje, akiwapa maagizo, akisema, "Msigeuke kufuata njia ya watu wa mataifa, wala msiingie mji wa Wasamaria;
sw.B: Yesu aliwatuma hao kumi na wawili, akawapa maagizo haya: "Msishike njia zinazoelekea kwa watu wa mataifa, wala msiingie mji wa Kisamaria.
sw.R: Yesu aliwatuma watu hao kumi na wawili. Kwanza aliwaeleza la kufanya: "Msiende kwa watu wasio Wayahudi. Wala msiingie mji wowote wanamoishi Wasamaria.

vi.L: Mười hai người này Đức Giê-xu đã sai đi, và truyền cho họ rằng: "Đừng đi vào đường của dân ngoại, và đừng vào thành nào của người Sa-ma-ri;
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu sai mười hai người ấy đi và dặn họ: "Đừng đi theo những con đường dẫn đến dân ngoại, và đừng vào thành nào của người Sa-ma-ri.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu sai mười hai người này đi. Trước khi họ đi, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dặn họ: "Đừng đến với những người không phải là người Do Thái. Cũng đừng vào thành nào có người Sa-ma-ri sống.

ko.L: 예수께서 이 열둘을 보내시면서 그들에게 지시하여 말씀하셨다. "이방 사람들의 길로 가지 말고, 사마리아 사람들의 고을에도 들어가지 마라.
ko.B: 예수께서 이 열두 제자를 보내시며 이렇게 명하셨다. "이방 사람들에게로 가는 길로 가지 말고, 사마리아 사람들의 고을에도 들어가지 마라.
ko.R: 예수께서 이 열두 제자를 보내셨다. 먼저 그들이 할 일을 일러 주셨다. "유대인이 아닌 사람들에게로 가지 마라. 사마리아 사람들이 사는 마을에도 들어가지 마라.

pt.L: A estes doze Jesus enviou, instruindo-os e dizendo: "Não tomem o caminho das nações e não entrem em cidade de samaritanos;
pt.B: Jesus enviou esses doze e lhes deu estas instruções: "Fiquem longe dos caminhos que levam aos não judeus, e não entrem em nenhuma cidade samaritana.
pt.R: Jesus enviou esses doze homens. Antes, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} explicou a eles o que deviam fazer: "Não vão até as pessoas que não são judias. E não entrem em nenhuma cidade onde moram samaritanos.

am.L: እነዚህን አሥራ ሁለቱን ኢየሱስ ሲልካቸው መመሪያ ሰጥቶ እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «የአሕዛብን መንገድ ይዛችሁ አትሂዱ፤ ወደ ሳምራውያን ከተማም አትግቡ፤
am.B: ኢየሱስ እነዚህን አሥራ ሁለቱን ላከ፤ እንዲህም ሲል አዘዛቸው፦ «ወደ አሕዛብ አገር ከሚወስዱ መንገዶች ራቁ፤ ወደ የትኛውም የሳምራውያን ከተማ አትግቡ።
am.R: ኢየሱስ እነዚህን አሥራ ሁለት ሰዎች ላካቸው። አስቀድሞም ምን ማድረግ እንዳለባቸው እንዲህ ብሎ ነገራቸው፦ «አይሁድ ወዳልሆኑ ሰዎች አትሂዱ። ሳምራውያን ወደሚኖሩበት ከተማም አትግቡ።

ru.L: Этих двенадцать послал Иисус, наставив их, говоря: «На путь язычников не уходите, и в город самаритян не входите;
ru.B: Этих двенадцать Иисус послал, дав им такие наставления: «Не ходите дорогами, ведущими к язычникам, и не заходите ни в один самаритянский город.
ru.R: Иисус послал этих двенадцать. Сначала {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} сказал им, что делать: «Не ходите к людям других народов. И не заходите в города, где живут самаритяне.

hi.L: इन बारहों को यीशु ने यह आज्ञा देकर भेजा, "अन्यजातियों के मार्ग पर न जाना, और सामरियों के किसी नगर में प्रवेश न करना;
hi.B: यीशु ने इन बारहों को भेजा, और उन्हें यह निर्देश दिया: "अन्यजातियों की ओर जानेवाले रास्तों से दूर रहना, और सामरियों के किसी नगर में न जाना।
hi.R: यीशु ने इन बारह आदमियों को भेजा। पहले उन्होंने उन्हें बताया कि क्या करना है: "ग़ैर-यहूदियों के पास मत जाना। और किसी ऐसे नगर में भी मत जाना जहाँ सामरी रहते हैं।

uk.L: Цих дванадцятьох послав Ісус, наказавши їм і кажучи: «На дорогу язичників не ходіть, і в місто самарян не входьте;
uk.B: Ісус послав цих дванадцятьох і настановив їх: «Не ходіть дорогами, що ведуть до язичників, і не заходьте в жодне самарянське місто.
uk.R: Ісус послав цих дванадцятьох. Спершу {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} пояснив їм, що робити: «Не йдіть до людей, які не є юдеями. І не заходьте в жодне місто, де живуть самаряни.

ja.L: イエスはこの十二人を遣わし、彼らに命じて言われた。「異邦人たちの道へ出て行ってはならない。サマリア人の町に入ってもならない。

ja.R: イエスは、この十二人を送り出されました。その前に、こう言いつけられました。「ユダヤ人でない人々のところへ行ってはいけない。サマリア人の住む町にも入ってはいけない。

decisions.choice: the road of the Gentiles: a road leading into Gentile country
decisions.reason: The words speak of a journey's direction. The twelve are not to take their mission beyond Israel.

decisions.choice: Samaritans: the people of Samaria, between Judea and Galilee
decisions.reason: The Samaritans worshiped the God of Israel but had their own temple and form of the law, and Jews and Samaritans were bitterly divided (John 4:9).

decisions.choice: a limit for this mission, not for all time
alternatives: a rule that the gospel is only for Israel
decisions.reason: Jesus comes first to Israel (15:24). After his resurrection he sends his disciples to all nations (28:19).

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Gentiles are, as in 4:15.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 10:42
alternatives: closing and reopening the quotation at each sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 5-42 are one speech, so the quotation marks stay open to the end.

decisions.choice: gentiles (L, B); gente que no es judía (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "gentiles" names the peoples who are not Israel; Readable says it plainly, as the English does (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every verb and pronoun addressed to the Twelve; the « opens here and stays open to the end of 10:42
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them, and English has no such choice. Jesus speaks from here to 10:42, so the words he quotes inside take “ ”, as the English puts them in single marks.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B); les gens qui ne sont pas juifs (R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 9): Literal keeps the Greek word's plain sense, Balanced says who is meant where the English says "Gentiles", and Readable follows the English Readable. "Les païens" now suggests unbelievers in general.

decisions.choice: watu wa mataifa (L, B); watu wasio Wayahudi (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for the peoples who are not Israel; Readable says it plainly, as the English does (meaning decision m1). Jesus speaks from here to 10:42, so the quotation stays open, and the words he quotes inside take single marks.

decisions.choice: "dân ngoại" (L, B); "những người không phải là người Do Thái" (R) for the Gentiles
decisions.reason: "dân ngoại" is the Bible word for the nations other than Israel; Readable says plainly who they are, as the English Readable does. The quotation that opens here runs to the end of 10:42.

decisions.choice: "열둘" (L), "열두 제자" (B, R); "이방 사람들" (L, B), "유대인이 아닌 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: As the addendum settles for the Gospels and the Korean Matthew 4:15. The quotation opens here and closes at the end of 10:42, as in the English.

decisions.choice: አሕዛብ (L, B); አይሁድ ያልሆኑ ሰዎች (R)
decisions.reason: አሕዛብ is the established word for the non-Jewish nations; Readable says plainly who they are, 'people who are not Jews', as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: “अन्यजाति” (L, B); “ग़ैर-यहूदी” (R)
decisions.reason: “अन्यजाति” is the established church word for the Gentiles; Readable says plainly who they are.

decisions.choice: "язычники" (L, B); "люди других народов" (R)
decisions.reason: Key term: Readable says who the Gentiles are, people who are not Jews.

decisions.choice: "язичники" (L, B); "люди, які не є юдеями" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled Ukrainian term for ethnē as non-Jews; Readable says in plain words who is meant.

decisions.choice: "異邦人の地へ向かう道" (B); "異邦人たちの道" (L); "ユダヤ人でない人々のところ" (R)
decisions.reason: The road of the Gentiles is a road leading into Gentile country (m1). Literal keeps the phrase, Balanced says where it leads, and Readable gives the Gentiles in everyday words, as the shared terms set.

decisions.choice: "〜てはならない" (L, B); "〜てはいけない" (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus instructs the twelve with authority in the plain style at every level; Readable uses the everyday form of prohibition. This holds for the charge that runs through 10:5-23.

ja.B: むしろ、失われた羊であるイスラエルの民のところへ行きなさい。

decisions.choice: the lost sheep, the house of Israel: the whole people is the lost flock
alternatives: only the lost ones within Israel
decisions.reason: As in 9:36, Jesus sees Israel as sheep without a shepherd. The same words come again in 15:24.

decisions.choice: lost sheep: Jeremiah 50:6; Ezekiel 34:4, 16
decisions.reason: The prophets call Israel lost sheep led astray by their shepherds, and God promises to seek the lost.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "House" means the whole family or nation.

decisions.choice: "chiên lạc mất" (L, B); "chiên đi lạc" (R)
decisions.reason: The picture of Jeremiah 50:6 and Ezekiel 34 (meaning decision), in the Bible's word for sheep, as in 9:36. The whole people is the lost flock, so Balanced and Readable name Israel itself.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘 집" (L); "이스라엘 백성" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The house of Israel is the whole people, the lost flock itself (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable say "people", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "загиблих" (L); "заблуканих", "що заблукали" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Apollymi covers both being lost and perishing; Literal keeps the stronger sense of the Greek word, Balanced and Readable the picture of sheep that have strayed.

decisions.choice: "イスラエルの家の失われた羊たち" (L); "失われた羊であるイスラエルの民" (B); "イスラエルの人々……迷子になった羊のようなものだ" (R), as in 15:24
alternatives: "イスラエルの家の失われた羊" (B)
decisions.reason: The whole house of Israel is the lost flock (m1); Balanced and Readable make that plain, as the English does, so it is not read as only the lost among Israel. Jesus uses the same words of himself in 15:24, and each level words them alike there.

source.text: πορευόμενοι δὲ κηρύσσετε λέγοντες ὅτι Ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Going and proclaim saying that, Has come near the kingdom of the heavens.

en.L: And as you go, proclaim, saying, 'The kingdom of the heavens has come near.'
en.B: Wherever you go, preach this: 'The kingdom of heaven has come near.'
en.R: As you travel, tell people, 'The kingdom of heaven is coming near.'

es.L: Y mientras {{plural_you:van|vais}}, {{plural_you:proclamen|proclamad}}, diciendo: “Se ha acercado el reino de los cielos”.
es.B: Por dondequiera que {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}}, {{plural_you:anuncien|anunciad}} esto: “El reino de los cielos se ha acercado”.
es.R: Mientras {{plural_you:viajan|viajáis}}, {{plural_you:digan|decid}} a la gente: “El reino de los cielos se está acercando”.

fr.L: Et en allant, proclamez, disant : “Le royaume des cieux s’est approché.”
fr.B: Partout où vous irez, prêchez ce message : “Le royaume des cieux est tout proche.”
fr.R: Pendant votre voyage, dites aux gens : “Le royaume des cieux s’approche.”

sw.L: Na mkienda, hubirini, mkisema, 'Ufalme wa mbinguni umekuja karibu.'
sw.B: Popote mwendapo, hubirini hivi: 'Ufalme wa mbinguni uko karibu.'
sw.R: Mnaposafiri, waambieni watu, 'Ufalme wa mbinguni unakaribia.'

vi.L: Và khi đi, hãy rao giảng rằng: 'Vương quốc thiên đàng đã đến gần.'
vi.B: Các con đi đến đâu, hãy rao giảng: 'Vương quốc thiên đàng đã đến gần.'
vi.R: Khi các con đi, hãy nói với mọi người: 'Vương quốc thiên đàng đang đến gần.'

ko.L: 가면서 선포하여 말하여라. '천국이 가까이 왔다.'
ko.B: 가는 곳마다 '천국이 가까이 왔다' 하고 선포하여라.
ko.R: 가는 곳마다 사람들에게 '천국이 가까이 오고 있다' 하고 전하여라.

pt.L: E, indo, proclamem, dizendo: 'O Reino dos céus se aproximou.'
pt.B: Por onde forem, preguem isto: 'O Reino dos céus está próximo.'
pt.R: Enquanto estiverem viajando, digam às pessoas: 'O Reino dos céus está chegando.'

am.L: ስትሄዱም “መንግሥተ ሰማያት ቀርባለች” እያላችሁ ስበኩ።
am.B: በምትሄዱበት ሁሉ “መንግሥተ ሰማያት ቀርባለች” ብላችሁ ስበኩ።
am.R: ስትጓዙ ለሰዎች “የሰማይ መንግሥት እየቀረበች ነው” ብላችሁ ንገሯቸው።

ru.L: Идя же, проповедуйте, говоря: “Приблизилось Царство Небесное”.
ru.B: Куда бы вы ни шли, возвещайте: “Царство Небесное приблизилось”.
ru.R: Когда будете идти по дорогам, говорите людям: “Небесное Царство уже близко”.

hi.L: और जाते हुए यह प्रचार करना कि 'स्वर्ग का राज्य निकट आ पहुँचा है।'
hi.B: जहाँ कहीं भी जाओ, यह प्रचार करो: 'स्वर्ग का राज्य पास आ गया है।'
hi.R: रास्ते में लोगों को बताओ, 'स्वर्ग का राज्य पास आ रहा है।'

uk.L: А йдучи, проповідуйте, кажучи: “Наблизилося Царство Небесне.”
uk.B: Куди б ви не йшли, проповідуйте: “Наблизилося Царство Небесне.”
uk.R: У дорозі кажіть людям: “Небесне Царство вже близько.”

ja.L: 行きながら、宣べ伝えて、『天の国は近づいた』と言いなさい。
ja.B: 行く先々で、『天の国は近づいた』と宣べ伝えなさい。
ja.R: 旅をしながら、人々に、『天の国は近づいている』と知らせなさい。

decisions.choice: the same message as John's and Jesus's (3:2; 4:17)
decisions.reason: The twelve announce what Jesus announced. See 3:2 on "the kingdom of heaven".

decisions.choice: the same wording as 4:17 at each level
decisions.reason: The repeated message is given in the same words.

decisions.choice: el reino de los cielos
decisions.reason: The term used throughout Matthew: Matthew's way of saying "the kingdom of God", keeping the plural of the Greek as Spanish usage does.

decisions.choice: le royaume des cieux, every level
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 9): the plural keeps Matthew's form, and the English keeps "kingdom of heaven" at Readable too.

decisions.choice: ufalme wa mbinguni
decisions.reason: The term used throughout Matthew, his way of saying "the kingdom of God". "Mbinguni" (in heaven) is the natural Swahili form.

decisions.choice: "vương quốc thiên đàng" at every level
decisions.reason: The phrase settled for Matthew; the message is the same as John's and Jesus's in 3:2 and 4:17 (meaning decision), so it is worded as there.

decisions.choice: "천국" at every level; the message worded as in the Korean Matthew 3:2 and 4:17
decisions.reason: The same message as John's and Jesus's (meaning decision). "천국" is the settled Korean term for Matthew's "kingdom of the heavens" at every level.

decisions.choice: መንግሥተ ሰማያት (L, B); የሰማይ መንግሥት (R)
decisions.reason: መንግሥተ ሰማያት, the Ge'ez phrase for 'the kingdom of the heavens', is the living church name for it and keeps the Greek plural, so Literal and Balanced use it; Readable says the same in plain Amharic, የሰማይ መንግሥት. Neither replaces 'heaven' with 'God', which Matthew's wording avoids.

decisions.choice: “स्वर्ग का राज्य”
decisions.reason: The key term is the same at every level; Hindi “स्वर्ग” already stands for the Greek plural “the heavens”, which here means God's realm, not the sky.

decisions.choice: "Царство Небесное" (L, B); "Небесное Царство" (R)
decisions.reason: Key term: Literal and Balanced keep the traditional order; Readable puts the adjective first, as everyday Russian does. "Heaven" here stands for God.

source.text: ἀσθενοῦντας θεραπεύετε, νεκροὺς ἐγείρετε, λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε, δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλετε· δωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε.

records.literal_gloss: Ailing heal, dead raise, lepers cleanse, demons cast out; freely you received, freely give.

en.L: Heal [the] sick, raise [the] dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. Freely you received; freely give.
en.B: Heal those who are sick, raise the dead, make lepers clean, drive out demons. You received without paying, so give without charging.
en.R: Heal sick people. Bring dead people back to life. Heal people who have skin diseases. Make demons leave people. You did not pay for what you were given, so do not ask people to pay you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sanen|Sanad}} enfermos, {{plural_you:resuciten|resucitad}} muertos, {{plural_you:limpien|limpiad}} leprosos, {{plural_you:expulsen|expulsad}} demonios. Gratis {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}}; {{plural_you:den|dad}} gratis.
es.B: {{plural_you:Sanen|Sanad}} a los enfermos, {{plural_you:resuciten|resucitad}} a los muertos, {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} limpios a los leprosos, {{plural_you:echen|echad}} fuera a los demonios. {{plural_you:Recibieron|Recibisteis}} sin pagar; {{plural_you:den|dad}} sin cobrar.
es.R: {{plural_you:Sanen|Sanad}} a los enfermos. {{plural_you:Devuelvan|Devolved}} la vida a los muertos. {{plural_you:Sanen|Sanad}} a los que tienen enfermedades de la piel. {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} salir a los demonios de la gente. {{plural_you:Ustedes no pagaron|Vosotros no pagasteis}} por lo que {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}}, así que no {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} a nadie que {{plural_you:les|os}} pague.

fr.L: Guérissez les malades, ressuscitez les morts, purifiez les lépreux, chassez les démons. Gratuitement vous avez reçu ; gratuitement donnez.
fr.B: Guérissez les malades, ressuscitez les morts, rendez purs les lépreux, chassez les démons. Vous avez reçu sans payer ; donnez sans faire payer.
fr.R: Guérissez les malades. Faites revenir les morts à la vie. Guérissez les gens qui ont des maladies de peau. Faites sortir les démons des gens. Vous n’avez rien payé pour ce que vous avez reçu, alors ne demandez pas aux gens de vous payer.

sw.L: Wagonjwa waponyeni, wafu wafufueni, wenye ukoma watakaseni, pepo wafukuzeni. Bila malipo mlipokea; bila malipo toeni.
sw.B: Waponyeni wagonjwa, wafufueni waliokufa, watakaseni wenye ukoma, wafukuzeni pepo. Mlipokea bila kulipa, kwa hiyo toeni bila kudai malipo.
sw.R: Waponyeni wagonjwa. Wafufueni waliokufa. Waponyeni watu wenye magonjwa ya ngozi. Wafukuzeni pepo watoke kwa watu. Hamkulipa kwa yale mliyopewa, kwa hiyo msiwadai watu malipo.

vi.L: Hãy chữa lành người đau yếu, khiến người chết sống lại, làm sạch người phung, đuổi các quỷ. Các con đã nhận không, hãy cho không.
vi.B: Hãy chữa lành người bệnh, khiến người chết sống lại, làm cho người phung được sạch, và đuổi quỷ. Các con đã nhận không phải trả gì, thì hãy cho đi mà không đòi gì.
vi.R: Hãy chữa lành người bệnh. Hãy làm cho người chết sống lại. Hãy chữa lành người bị bệnh phong. Hãy đuổi quỷ ra khỏi người ta. Các con đã nhận được những điều này mà không phải trả tiền, thì đừng đòi người ta trả tiền cho các con.

ko.L: 앓는 사람들을 고치고, 죽은 사람들을 살리고, 나병 환자들을 깨끗하게 하고, 귀신들을 쫓아내어라. 너희가 거저 받았으니, 거저 주어라.
ko.B: 병든 사람들을 고쳐 주고, 죽은 사람들을 살리고, 악성 피부병에 걸린 사람들을 깨끗하게 하고, 귀신을 쫓아내어라. 너희가 값없이 받았으니, 값없이 주어라.
ko.R: 아픈 사람들을 고쳐 주어라. 죽은 사람들을 다시 살려 주어라. 심한 피부병을 앓는 사람들을 깨끗하게 고쳐 주어라. 사람들에게서 귀신을 쫓아내어라. 너희는 돈을 내지 않고 받았다. 그러니 사람들에게 돈을 받지 말고 거저 주어라.

pt.L: Curem doentes, ressuscitem mortos, purifiquem leprosos, expulsem demônios. De graça vocês receberam; de graça deem.
pt.B: Curem os doentes, ressuscitem os mortos, purifiquem os leprosos, expulsem os demônios. Vocês receberam sem pagar; então deem sem cobrar.
pt.R: Curem as pessoas doentes. Façam os mortos voltarem à vida. Curem as pessoas que têm doenças de pele. Façam os demônios saírem das pessoas. Vocês não pagaram pelo que receberam, então não peçam que as pessoas paguem a vocês.

am.L: ሕመምተኞችን ፈውሱ፣ ሙታንን አስነሡ፣ ለምጻሞችን አንጹ፣ አጋንንትን አስወጡ። በነጻ ተቀበላችሁ፤ በነጻ ስጡ።
am.B: የታመሙትን ፈውሱ፤ የሞቱትን አስነሡ፤ ለምጽ ያለባቸውን አንጹ፤ አጋንንትን አስወጡ። ያለ ክፍያ ተቀበላችሁ፤ ያለ ክፍያም ስጡ።
am.R: የታመሙ ሰዎችን ፈውሱ። የሞቱ ሰዎችን ወደ ሕይወት መልሱ። የቆዳ በሽታ ያለባቸውን ሰዎች ፈውሱ። አጋንንትን ከሰዎች አስወጡ። የተሰጣችሁን ያገኛችሁት ሳትከፍሉ ነው፤ ስለዚህ ሰዎች እንዲከፍሏችሁ አትጠይቁ።

ru.L: Больных исцеляйте, мёртвых воскрешайте, прокажённых очищайте, бесов изгоняйте. Даром получили — даром давайте.
ru.B: Исцеляйте больных, воскрешайте мёртвых, очищайте прокажённых, изгоняйте бесов. Вы получили бесплатно — бесплатно и давайте.
ru.R: Исцеляйте больных людей. Возвращайте к жизни умерших. Исцеляйте людей, у которых кожные болезни. Выгоняйте из людей бесов. Вы ничего не платили за то, что получили, поэтому и с людей ничего не берите.

hi.L: बीमारों को चंगा करो, मरे हुओं को जिलाओ, कोढ़ियों को शुद्ध करो, दुष्टात्माओं को निकालो। तुमने मुफ़्त में पाया है, मुफ़्त में दो।
hi.B: बीमारों को चंगा करो, मरे हुओं को जिला उठाओ, कोढ़ियों को शुद्ध करो, दुष्टात्माओं को निकालो। तुमने बिना दाम चुकाए पाया है, इसलिए बिना दाम लिए दो।
hi.R: बीमार लोगों को चंगा करो। मरे हुए लोगों को फिर से ज़िंदा करो। चमड़ी के रोगवाले लोगों को ठीक करो। दुष्टात्माओं को लोगों में से निकालो। तुमने जो पाया उसके लिए कुछ नहीं चुकाया, इसलिए लोगों से भी कुछ मत माँगना।

uk.L: Недужих зцілюйте, мертвих воскрешайте, прокажених очищайте, бісів виганяйте. Даром ви отримали, даром давайте.
uk.B: Зцілюйте хворих, воскрешайте мертвих, очищайте прокажених, виганяйте бісів. Ви отримали задарма — задарма й давайте.
uk.R: Лікуйте хворих. Повертайте мертвих до життя. Лікуйте людей, які мають тяжкі шкірні хвороби. Виганяйте з людей бісів. Ви нічого не платили за те, що отримали, тож і з людей нічого не беріть.

ja.L: 病んでいる者たちを癒やし、死者たちを起こし、重い皮膚病の者たちを清め、悪霊たちを追い出しなさい。あなたがたはただで受けた。ただで与えなさい。
ja.B: 病人を癒やし、死者を生き返らせ、重い皮膚病の人を清め、悪霊を追い出しなさい。あなたがたは代価を払わずに受けたのだから、代価を求めずに与えなさい。
ja.R: 病気の人をいやしなさい。死んだ人を生き返らせなさい。重い皮膚の病気の人を治しなさい。悪霊を人から追い出しなさい。あなたたちは、お金を払わずにもらった。だから、人からお金を取ってはいけない。

decisions.choice: cleanse lepers: heal skin diseases that made a person unclean
alternatives: leprosy in the modern medical sense only
decisions.reason: As in 8:2-3, the word covered several skin diseases. Healing also made the person clean, able to return to worship and community.

decisions.choice: freely: as a gift, without payment
decisions.reason: The twelve received their power from Jesus at no cost, so they must not sell it. Compare Acts 8:18-20.

decisions.choice: raise the dead, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words are missing in many later manuscripts, and their place varies in others
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts lack "raise the dead", and others place it differently in the list. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: people who have skin diseases
decisions.reason: Readable describes the condition, as in 8:2.

decisions.choice: objects first: Wagonjwa waponyeni, wafu wafufueni
decisions.reason: Swahili can put the object first, with the object prefix in the verb, so Literal keeps the Greek order, where each command begins with the people it is for.

decisions.choice: "người phung" (L, B); "người bị bệnh phong" (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:2: skin diseases that made a person unclean (meaning decision). "làm sạch" keeps the Greek verb at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "chữa lành".

decisions.choice: "나병 환자" (L); "악성 피부병에 걸린 사람" (B); "심한 피부병을 앓는 사람" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Matthew 8:2 and Mark 1:40: the word covered several skin diseases that made a person unclean (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "거저" (L); "값없이" (B); spelled out (R)
decisions.reason: Freely means as a gift, without payment (meaning decision). "값없이" is the natural word for a gift given without price; Readable says what it means for them.

decisions.choice: "прокажённые" (L, B); "люди, у которых кожные болезни" (R)
decisions.reason: The word covered skin diseases that made a person unclean, not only leprosy; Readable describes the condition.

decisions.choice: "重い皮膚病" (L, B); "重い皮膚の病気" (R)
decisions.reason: The word covered several skin diseases that made a person unclean (m1), not only Hansen's disease; as in Mark 1:40, Japanese avoids the older name. Healing also made them clean, so Literal and Balanced keep "清め".

decisions.choice: "ただで" (L); "代価を払わずに……代価を求めずに" (B); "お金を払わずに……お金を取ってはいけない" (R)
decisions.reason: Freely means as a gift, without payment (m2). Literal keeps the two short clauses side by side as in the Greek; Balanced and Readable say what is received and what must not be charged.

source.text: μὴ κτήσησθε χρυσὸν μηδὲ ἄργυρον μηδὲ χαλκὸν εἰς τὰς ζώνας ὑμῶν, μὴ πήραν εἰς ὁδὸν μηδὲ δύο χιτῶνας μηδὲ ὑποδήματα μηδὲ ῥάβδον· ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Not acquire gold nor silver nor copper in the belts of you, \v 10 not a bag for road nor two tunics nor sandals nor a staff; worthy for the worker of the food of him.

en.L: Do not acquire gold or silver or copper for your belts, \v 10 nor a bag for [the] road, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for the worker [is] worthy of {{gender:their|his}} food.
en.B: Do not provide yourselves with money for your belts, whether gold, silver, or copper. \v 10 Take no bag for the road, no second tunic, no sandals, and no staff. Workers have earned their food.
en.R: Do not take any money with you, not gold or silver or even copper coins. \v 10 Do not take a bag for the trip, or extra clothes, or sandals, or a walking stick. People who work should be given food. The people you serve will take care of you.

es.L: No {{plural_you:adquieran|adquiráis}} oro, ni plata, ni cobre para {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cinturones, \v 10 ni alforja para [el] camino, ni dos túnicas, ni sandalias, ni bastón; pues digno [es] el trabajador de su sustento.
es.B: No {{plural_you:se procuren|os procuréis}} dinero para el cinturón, sea oro, plata o cobre. \v 10 No {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} bolsa para el viaje, ni túnica de repuesto, ni sandalias, ni bastón. Quien trabaja se ha ganado su comida.
es.R: No {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} dinero, ni oro, ni plata, ni siquiera monedas de cobre. \v 10 No {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} bolsa para el viaje, ni ropa de repuesto, ni sandalias, ni bastón para caminar. Al que trabaja se le debe dar de comer. La gente a la que {{plural_you:sirvan|sirváis}} se ocupará de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Ne vous procurez ni or, ni argent, ni cuivre pour vos ceintures, \v 10 ni sac pour la route, ni deux tuniques, ni sandales, ni bâton ; car l’ouvrier est digne de sa nourriture.
fr.B: N’emportez dans vos ceintures aucune monnaie, ni or, ni argent, ni cuivre. \v 10 Ne prenez ni sac pour la route, ni seconde tunique, ni sandales, ni bâton. Les ouvriers méritent leur nourriture.
fr.R: Ne prenez pas d’argent avec vous : pas de pièces d’or, pas de pièces d’argent, pas même de pièces de cuivre. \v 10 Ne prenez pas de sac pour le voyage, ni de vêtements de rechange, ni de sandales, ni de bâton de marche. Ceux qui travaillent doivent recevoir de quoi manger. Les gens que vous servirez s’occuperont de vous.

sw.L: Msijipatie dhahabu wala fedha wala shaba katika mikanda yenu, \v 10 wala mkoba kwa ajili ya njia, wala mavazi ya ndani mawili, wala viatu, wala fimbo; kwa maana mfanyakazi anastahili chakula chake.
sw.B: Msijipatie pesa za kuweka mikandani mwenu, iwe dhahabu, fedha au shaba. \v 10 Msichukue mkoba wa safari, wala vazi la pili, wala viatu, wala fimbo. Mfanyakazi amestahili chakula chake.
sw.R: Msichukue pesa yoyote, iwe dhahabu, fedha, au hata sarafu za shaba. \v 10 Msichukue mkoba wa safari, wala nguo za ziada, wala viatu, wala fimbo ya kutembelea. Watu wanaofanya kazi wanapaswa kupewa chakula. Watu mnaowahudumia watawatunza.

vi.L: Đừng kiếm vàng, bạc, hay đồng [để bỏ] trong thắt lưng các con, \v 10 đừng [mang] bao bị đi đường, đừng [mang] hai áo, đừng [mang] dép, cũng đừng [mang] gậy; vì người làm công đáng được thức ăn của mình.
vi.B: Đừng lo mang theo tiền trong thắt lưng, dù là vàng, bạc hay đồng. \v 10 Đừng mang túi hành lý đi đường, đừng mang áo thứ hai, đừng mang dép, cũng đừng mang gậy. Người làm công đáng được nuôi ăn.
vi.R: Đừng mang theo tiền bạc gì cả, dù là vàng, bạc hay chỉ là mấy đồng xu. \v 10 Đừng mang túi xách khi đi đường, đừng mang thêm áo, đừng mang dép hay gậy. Người làm việc thì đáng được cho ăn. Những người các con giúp đỡ sẽ lo cho các con.

ko.L: 너희 허리띠에 금이나 은이나 동전을 마련하지 말고, \v 10 길을 [갈 때] 자루나 속옷 두 벌이나 신발이나 지팡이도 [마련하지 마라]. 일꾼이 자기 먹을 것을 받는 것은 마땅하기 때문이다.
ko.B: 허리띠에 금화나 은화나 동전을 넣어 가지 마라. \v 10 여행할 때에 자루도, 여벌 옷도, 신발도, 지팡이도 가지고 가지 마라. 일꾼은 자기 먹을 것을 얻을 자격이 있다.
ko.R: 돈을 가지고 가지 마라. 금이나 은은 물론 작은 동전도 가지고 가지 마라. \v 10 여행 가방도, 갈아입을 옷도, 신발도, 지팡이도 가지고 가지 마라. 일하는 사람은 먹을 것을 받아야 마땅하다. 너희가 섬기는 사람들이 너희를 돌보아 줄 것이다.

pt.L: Não adquiram ouro, nem prata, nem cobre para os cintos de vocês, \v 10 nem bolsa para o caminho, nem duas túnicas, nem sandálias, nem cajado; pois digno [é] o trabalhador do seu alimento.
pt.B: Não se abasteçam de dinheiro para levar no cinto, seja ouro, prata ou cobre. \v 10 Não levem bolsa para a viagem, nem uma túnica a mais, nem sandálias, nem cajado. Quem trabalha merece o seu alimento.
pt.R: Não levem dinheiro nenhum, nem ouro, nem prata, nem mesmo moedas de cobre. \v 10 Não levem bolsa para a viagem, nem roupa extra, nem sandálias, nem cajado. Quem trabalha deve receber comida. As pessoas a quem vocês servirem vão cuidar de vocês.

am.L: ለመቀነታችሁ ወርቅ ወይም ብር ወይም ናስ አታግኙ፤ \v 10 ለመንገድም ስልቻ፣ ወይም ሁለት እጀ ጠባብ፣ ወይም ጫማ፣ ወይም በትር [አትያዙ]፤ ሠራተኛ ምግቡ ይገባዋልና።
am.B: ለመቀነታችሁ ገንዘብ አትያዙ፤ ወርቅም ቢሆን ብርም ቢሆን ናስም ቢሆን። \v 10 ለመንገድ ስልቻ፣ ተጨማሪ እጀ ጠባብ፣ ጫማ ወይም በትር አትያዙ። ሠራተኛ ምግቡን ሊያገኝ ይገባዋል።
am.R: ምንም ገንዘብ ይዛችሁ አትሂዱ፤ ወርቅ ወይም ብር ወይም የናስ ሳንቲም እንኳ አትያዙ። \v 10 ለጉዞው ስልቻ፣ ወይም ተጨማሪ ልብስ፣ ወይም ጫማ፣ ወይም ምርኩዝ አትያዙ። የሚሠራ ሰው ምግብ ሊሰጠው ይገባል። የምታገለግሏቸው ሰዎች ይንከባከቧችኋል።

ru.L: Не приобретайте ни золота, ни серебра, ни меди в пояса ваши, \v 10 ни сумы на дорогу, ни двух рубах, ни сандалий, ни посоха; ведь достоин работник своего пропитания.
ru.B: Не запасайтесь деньгами в поясах — ни золотом, ни серебром, ни медью. \v 10 Не берите ни сумы в дорогу, ни второй рубашки, ни сандалий, ни посоха. Работник заслужил свою еду.
ru.R: Не берите с собой денег — ни золотых, ни серебряных, ни даже медных монет. \v 10 Не берите в дорогу ни сумки, ни запасной одежды, ни сандалий, ни палки. Тот, кто работает, должен получать еду. Люди, которым вы служите, позаботятся о вас.

hi.L: अपने कमरबंदों के लिए न सोना, न चाँदी, न ताँबा जुटाना, \v 10 न रास्ते के लिए झोला, न दो कुरते, न जूतियाँ, न लाठी; क्योंकि मज़दूर अपने भोजन का हक़दार है।
hi.B: अपने कमरबंद में पैसे न रखना, चाहे सोना हो, चाँदी हो या ताँबा। \v 10 रास्ते के लिए न झोला लेना, न दूसरा कुरता, न जूतियाँ, न लाठी। मज़दूर अपने भोजन का हक़दार है।
hi.R: अपने साथ कोई पैसा मत ले जाना, न सोना, न चाँदी, न ताँबे के सिक्के भी। \v 10 यात्रा के लिए न झोला लेना, न ज़्यादा कपड़े, न जूतियाँ, न चलने की लाठी। जो काम करते हैं उन्हें खाना मिलना चाहिए। जिन लोगों की तुम सेवा करोगे, वे तुम्हारी देखभाल करेंगे।

uk.L: Не набувайте ні золота, ні срібла, ні міді у ваші пояси, \v 10 ні торби на дорогу, ні двох хітонів, ні сандалів, ні палиці; бо вартий робітник своєї їжі.
uk.B: Не беріть із собою грошей у пояси — ні золота, ні срібла, ні міді. \v 10 Не беріть торби на дорогу, ні другої сорочки, ні сандалів, ні палиці. Робітник заслуговує на свою їжу.
uk.R: Не беріть із собою грошей — ні золотих, ні срібних, ні навіть мідних монет. \v 10 Не беріть торби в дорогу, ні запасного одягу, ні сандалів, ні палиці. Тим, хто працює, треба давати їжу. Люди, яким ви служите, подбають про вас.

ja.L: あなたがたの帯の中に、金も銀も銅も用意してはならない。\v 10 旅のための袋も、二枚の下着も、サンダルも、杖も[用意してはならない]。働き手は自分の食べ物に値するからである。
ja.B: 帯の中にお金を用意して行ってはならない。金貨も銀貨も銅貨もである。\v 10 旅の袋も、着替えの下着も、サンダルも、杖も持って行ってはならない。働く人には、食べ物を受ける資格がある。
ja.R: お金は持って行ってはいけない。金も銀も、小さな銅貨さえもだ。\v 10 旅の袋も、着がえの服も、サンダルも、杖も持って行ってはいけない。働く人は、食べ物をもらってよいのだ。あなたたちが仕える人々が、あなたたちの世話をしてくれる。

decisions.choice: acquire: get or provide for yourselves for the journey
decisions.reason: The verb means to get or procure. With 10:8 it may also forbid making money from the mission, but the list that follows is about what to take.

decisions.choice: gold, silver, copper in your belts: money of any kind
decisions.reason: Coins were carried in a fold of the belt. Copper coins were the smallest change, so the list rules out money altogether.

decisions.choice: a bag, a second tunic, a staff: the gear of a traveler
decisions.reason: A traveler carried a bag for food, a spare tunic for the cold, and a staff for walking and defense. Mark 6:8-9 allows a staff and sandals; Matthew and Luke 9:3 have Jesus forbid them. Each Gospel stresses that the twelve are to travel light and depend on God.

decisions.choice: the worker is worthy of his food: those they serve should feed them
alternatives: they must earn food by other work
decisions.reason: This is the reason for going without supplies. Luke 10:7 has "wages", and Paul cites the saying (1 Corinthians 9:14; 1 Timothy 5:18).

decisions.choice: The people you serve will take care of you.
decisions.reason: Readable states how the saying applies to the twelve.

decisions.choice: su sustento, su comida, with no gender span
decisions.reason: English needs a gender span for "their" or "his" food; Spanish "su" serves for a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "sa nourriture" with no gender span (L)
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs {{gender:their|his}}; the French possessive "sa" agrees with "nourriture" and says nothing of the worker's sex, so no setting is needed, as in Luke 10:7.

decisions.choice: mfanyakazi ... chakula chake, with no gender span
decisions.reason: English needs a gender span for "their" or "his" food; Swahili "mfanyakazi" and "chake" serve for a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "người làm công đáng được thức ăn của mình" (L) with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal puts "their/his" under the gender setting; Vietnamese "người làm công" and "mình" already include men and women, so there is nothing for a setting to switch.

decisions.choice: "속옷" (L); "여벌 옷" (B); "갈아입을 옷" (R) for the tunic
decisions.reason: As the Korean Mark 6:9: "속옷" is the Korean John's word for the tunic worn next to the body (19:23); today it suggests underwear, so Balanced and Readable say what was forbidden, a second set of clothes.

decisions.choice: "[마련하지 마라]" (L)
alternatives: leaving the list without a verb
decisions.reason: The Greek lets the one verb "acquire" govern the whole list across the verse break; Korean needs the verb at the end of each clause, so Literal repeats it in brackets in 10:10, which keeps each verse's content after its marker.

decisions.choice: do seu alimento, with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender setting on the possessive
decisions.reason: The English needs a setting to choose between "their" and "his". Portuguese "seu" agrees with "alimento", not with the worker, so it says nothing about the worker's sex and no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: ሠራተኛ ምግቡ ይገባዋል, with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span, as the English Literal has for 'their' or 'his' food
decisions.reason: Amharic speaks of a worker in general with the ordinary singular, ሠራተኛ ... ምግቡ, which is heard as any worker, man or woman; there is no second wording for a setting to switch to.

decisions.choice: መቀነት (belt, sash); እጀ ጠባብ (tunic)
decisions.reason: The money was carried in the folds of a cloth belt, which is what a መቀነት is; እጀ ጠባብ is the traditional word for the long shirt worn under the cloak.

decisions.choice: “अपने भोजन” with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: The Hindi reflexive “अपने” is the same for women and men, so there is no second wording for the setting to offer. The same holds for “मनुष्य”, “लोग” and “कोई” in this passage.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "своего пропитания" (L); "люди" (10:17)
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Where the English has a gender span (here and on "people" in 10:17), Russian is already inclusive: the reflexive "свой" has no gender, and "люди" means men and women. So the Russian has no span (for the whole passage).

decisions.choice: "рубаха" (L); "рубашка" (B)
decisions.reason: The tunic was the garment worn next to the body; "хитон" is a word for specialists.

decisions.choice: "робітник своєї їжі" with no gender span, where the English Literal has {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The Ukrainian reflexive "свій" has no gender, so the setting has nothing to change; likewise "людей" in 10:17 is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: "хітон" (L); "сорочка" (B)
decisions.reason: The chitōn was the long shirt worn under the cloak; Literal keeps the Greek word, Balanced names its everyday counterpart.

decisions.choice: "自分の食べ物" with no gender span (L)
decisions.reason: The English Literal puts the worker's pronoun under the gender setting. Japanese "自分の" names no gender, so no span is needed.

decisions.choice: "二枚の下着" (L); "着替えの下着" (B); "着がえの服" (R)
decisions.reason: The tunic was worn under the cloak, and a traveler carried a spare (m3). The words follow Mark 6:9; Balanced and Readable say it was a change of clothes.

source.text: εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν πόλιν ἢ κώμην εἰσέλθητε, ἐξετάσατε τίς ἐν αὐτῇ ἄξιός ἐστιν· κἀκεῖ μείνατε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε.

records.literal_gloss: Into whatever now town or village you enter, inquire who in it worthy is; and there remain until you go out.

en.L: And into whatever town or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and stay there until you go out.
en.B: When you go into a town or village, ask who in it is worthy, and stay with that person until you move on.
en.R: When you come to a town or village, find someone there who is ready to welcome you. Stay in that person's home until you leave that place.

es.L: Y en cualquier ciudad o aldea en que {{plural_you:entren|entréis}}, {{plural_you:averigüen|averiguad}} quién en ella es digno, y {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} allí hasta que {{plural_you:salgan|salgáis}}.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en una ciudad o aldea, {{plural_you:pregunten|preguntad}} quién es digno allí, y {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} en su casa hasta que {{plural_you:se vayan|os vayáis}}.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:lleguen|lleguéis}} a una ciudad o aldea, {{plural_you:busquen|buscad}} a alguien que esté dispuesto a {{plural_you:recibirlos|recibiros}}. {{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} en su casa hasta que {{plural_you:salgan|salgáis}} de ese lugar.

fr.L: Et dans quelque ville ou village que vous entriez, informez-vous de qui y est digne, et demeurez là jusqu’à ce que vous partiez.
fr.B: Quand vous entrerez dans une ville ou un village, cherchez qui y est digne, et restez chez lui jusqu’à ce que vous repartiez.
fr.R: Quand vous arrivez dans une ville ou un village, cherchez quelqu’un qui est prêt à vous accueillir. Restez dans sa maison jusqu’à ce que vous quittiez cet endroit.

sw.L: Na mji au kijiji chochote mtakachoingia, ulizeni ni nani ndani yake anayestahili; na hapo kaeni hadi mtakapoondoka.
sw.B: Mkiingia katika mji au kijiji, ulizeni ni nani humo anayestahili, mkae kwake mpaka mtakapoendelea na safari.
sw.R: Mkifika katika mji au kijiji, mtafuteni mtu aliye tayari kuwakaribisha. Kaeni nyumbani kwake mpaka mtakapoondoka mahali hapo.

vi.L: Và khi các con vào thành hay làng nào, hãy dò hỏi xem trong đó ai là người xứng đáng; và hãy ở lại đó cho đến khi các con đi.
vi.B: Khi các con vào một thành hay một làng, hãy tìm hỏi xem ở đó ai là người xứng đáng, rồi ở lại nhà người ấy cho đến khi các con đi nơi khác.
vi.R: Khi các con đến một thành hay một làng, hãy tìm một người sẵn lòng tiếp đón các con. Hãy ở lại nhà người ấy cho đến khi các con rời nơi đó.

ko.L: 너희가 어느 도시나 마을에 들어가든지, 그 안에 누가 합당한 사람인지 알아보아라. 그리고 너희가 떠날 때까지 거기에 머물러라.
ko.B: 어느 도시나 마을에 들어가든지, 그곳에서 누가 너희를 맞아들일 만한 사람인지 알아보아라. 그리고 그곳을 떠날 때까지 그 사람의 집에 머물러라.
ko.R: 어느 도시나 마을에 가든지, 너희를 기꺼이 맞아 줄 사람을 찾아라. 그리고 그곳을 떠날 때까지 그 사람의 집에서 지내라.

pt.L: E em qualquer cidade ou povoado em que entrarem, procurem saber quem nela é digno, e fiquem ali até saírem.
pt.B: Quando entrarem numa cidade ou num povoado, perguntem quem ali é digno, e fiquem com essa pessoa até partirem.
pt.R: Quando chegarem a uma cidade ou a um povoado, procurem alguém que esteja pronto para receber vocês. Fiquem na casa dessa pessoa até saírem daquele lugar.

am.L: ወደምትገቡባትም ከተማ ወይም መንደር ሁሉ፣ በእርሷ ውስጥ ብቁ የሆነው ማን እንደ ሆነ መርምሩ፤ እስክትወጡም ድረስ በዚያ ቆዩ።
am.B: ወደ አንድ ከተማ ወይም መንደር በገባችሁ ጊዜ በዚያ ያለውን ብቁ ሰው ጠይቃችሁ ፈልጉ፤ ከዚያ ስፍራ እስክትሄዱም ድረስ በእርሱ ቤት ቆዩ።
am.R: ወደ አንድ ከተማ ወይም መንደር ስትደርሱ እናንተን ለመቀበል ፈቃደኛ የሆነ ሰው ፈልጉ። ከዚያ ስፍራ እስክትሄዱ ድረስ በዚያ ሰው ቤት ቆዩ።

ru.L: В какой же город или селение войдёте, разузнайте, кто в нём достоин, и там оставайтесь, пока не выйдете.
ru.B: Когда придёте в какой-нибудь город или селение, узнайте, кто там достоин, и оставайтесь у этого человека, пока не пойдёте дальше.
ru.R: Когда придёте в город или в село, найдите там человека, который готов принять вас. Живите в его доме, пока не уйдёте из этого места.

hi.L: और जिस किसी नगर या गाँव में तुम प्रवेश करो, पता लगाओ कि उसमें कौन योग्य है, और जब तक वहाँ से न निकलो, उसी के यहाँ ठहरे रहो।
hi.B: जब तुम किसी नगर या गाँव में जाओ, तो पता करो कि वहाँ कौन योग्य है, और आगे बढ़ने तक उसी के घर ठहरो।
hi.R: जब तुम किसी नगर या गाँव में पहुँचो, तो वहाँ किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति को ढूँढो जो तुम्हारा स्वागत करने को तैयार हो। जब तक तुम उस जगह से न जाओ, उसी के घर में रहो।

uk.L: А в яке б місто чи село ви не ввійшли, розпитайте, хто в ньому гідний, і там залишайтеся, доки не вийдете.
uk.B: Коли ввійдете в місто чи село, розпитайте, хто там гідний, і залишайтеся в нього, доки не підете далі.
uk.R: Коли прийдете в місто чи село, знайдіть там людину, яка готова вас прийняти. Живіть у її домі, доки не підете з того місця.

ja.L: どの町や村に入っても、そこでだれがふさわしい者かを調べ、そこを出て行くまで、そこにとどまりなさい。
ja.B: 町や村に入ったら、そこでだれがふさわしい人かを尋ね、そこを去るまで、その人のところにとどまりなさい。
ja.R: 町や村に着いたら、あなたたちを喜んで迎えてくれる人を探しなさい。そして、その町を出るまで、その人の家に泊まっていなさい。

decisions.choice: worthy: open to the message and ready to receive the messengers
decisions.reason: The worthy house is the one that receives them and their words (10:13-14).

decisions.choice: stay there: do not move from house to house
decisions.reason: They are to lodge in one home for their whole stay in that place.

decisions.choice: someone ... who is ready to welcome you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "worthy" means here.

decisions.choice: "người sẵn lòng tiếp đón các con" (R) for "worthy"
decisions.reason: Worthy means open to the message and ready to receive the messengers (meaning decision); Readable says so, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "합당한 사람" (L); "맞아들일 만한 사람" (B); "기꺼이 맞아 줄 사람" (R); "머무르다" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Worthy means open to the message and ready to receive the messengers (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable say so. "머무르다" is the style guide's word for this verb, as in the Korean Mark 6:10.

decisions.choice: ብቁ (worthy)
decisions.reason: ብቁ, 'fit, worthy', is used for this Greek word through the chapter (10:11-13, 10:37-38), so the reader can follow it; የሚገባው can also mean 'the one who enters', which is confusing beside a verb of entering.

decisions.choice: "ふさわしい" (L, B); "あなたたちを喜んで迎えてくれる人" (R)
decisions.reason: The worthy are those open to the message and ready to receive the messengers (m1); Readable says so, as the English Readable does.

source.text: εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ἀσπάσασθε αὐτήν·

records.literal_gloss: Entering now into the house greet it;

en.L: And as you enter the house, greet it;
en.B: As you go into the home, greet the family.
en.R: When you go into a home, say, 'Peace be with you.'

es.L: Y al entrar en la casa, {{plural_you:salúdenla|saludadla}};
es.B: Al entrar en la casa, {{plural_you:saluden|saludad}} a la familia.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en una casa, {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: “La paz sea con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}”.

fr.L: Et en entrant dans la maison, saluez-la ;
fr.B: Quand vous entrerez dans une maison, saluez ceux qui y vivent.
fr.R: Quand vous entrez dans une maison, dites : “Que la paix soit avec vous !”

sw.L: Na mnapoingia katika nyumba, isalimuni;
sw.B: Mnapoingia nyumbani, wasalimuni watu wa nyumba hiyo.
sw.R: Mnapoingia katika nyumba, semeni, 'Amani iwe nanyi.'

vi.L: Và khi vào nhà, hãy chào nhà ấy;
vi.B: Khi vào nhà, hãy chào chúc gia đình ấy.
vi.R: Khi các con vào một nhà, hãy nói: 'Chúc bình an cho nhà này.'

ko.L: 그리고 그 집에 들어가면서 그 [집에] 인사하여라.
ko.B: 그 집에 들어갈 때에 그 집 식구들에게 인사하여라.
ko.R: 어떤 집에 들어갈 때에는 '이 집에 평안이 있기를 빕니다' 하고 인사하여라.

pt.L: E, ao entrarem na casa, saúdem-na;
pt.B: Ao entrarem na casa, saúdem a família.
pt.R: Quando entrarem numa casa, digam: 'Que a paz esteja com vocês.'

am.L: ወደ ቤቱም ስትገቡ ሰላምታ አቅርቡለት፤
am.B: ወደ ቤት ስትገቡ ለቤተሰቡ ሰላምታ አቅርቡ።
am.R: ወደ አንድ ቤት ስትገቡ “ሰላም ለእናንተ ይሁን” በሉ።

ru.L: Входя же в дом, приветствуйте его;
ru.B: Входя в дом, приветствуйте его обитателей.
ru.R: Когда входите в дом, говорите: “Мир вам”.

hi.L: और घर में जाते हुए उसे शुभकामना देना;
hi.B: घर में जाते समय उस परिवार को शुभकामना देना।
hi.R: जब तुम किसी घर में जाओ, तो कहना, 'इस घर पर शान्ति हो।'

uk.L: А входячи в дім, вітайте його;
uk.B: Заходячи в дім, привітайте родину.
uk.R: Коли заходите в дім, кажіть: “Мир вам.”

ja.L: その家に入るときには、その家にあいさつしなさい。
ja.B: 家に入るときには、その家の人々にあいさつしなさい。
ja.R: 家に入るときには、『この家に平安がありますように』とあいさつしなさい。

decisions.choice: the house: the household, the people who live there
decisions.reason: A greeting is given to people, as 10:13 shows.

decisions.choice: greet it, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: some manuscripts add "saying, Peace to this house"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts add the words of the greeting, as in Luke 10:5. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: say, 'Peace be with you'
decisions.reason: The usual greeting was a wish for peace, as 10:13 implies. Readable gives it.

decisions.choice: "Chúc bình an cho nhà này" (R)
decisions.reason: The greeting was a blessing of peace (meaning decision on 10:13); Readable gives the words, as the English Readable does, so 10:13 makes sense.

decisions.choice: "그 집 식구들에게" (B); the greeting of peace spelled out (R)
decisions.reason: The house is the household (meaning decision); Balanced names the family, and Readable gives the words of the greeting, as the English Readable does. The greeting is in 합쇼체, as one greets a household one is visiting.

decisions.choice: "その家の人々に" (B); "『この家に平安がありますように』" (R)
decisions.reason: The house means the household (m1), and the greeting is the blessing of peace that 10:13 speaks of; Readable gives its words, as the English Readable does, with "平安", the key-term word for peace as a greeting.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν μὲν ᾖ ἡ οἰκία ἀξία, ἐλθάτω ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν ἐπ’ αὐτήν· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ ἀξία, ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιστραφήτω.

records.literal_gloss: And if indeed be the house worthy, let come the peace of you upon it; if but not it be worthy, the peace of you to you let return.

en.L: And if the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
en.B: If that household is worthy, let your peace come to rest on it. But if it is unworthy, let the peace you gave come back to you.
en.R: If the people in that home welcome you, your blessing of peace will stay with them. If they do not welcome you, your blessing will come back to you.

es.L: Y si la casa es digna, venga sobre ella {{plural_you:la paz de ustedes|vuestra paz}}; pero si no es digna, {{plural_you:la paz de ustedes|vuestra paz}} vuelva a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Si esa familia es digna, que repose sobre ella la paz que {{plural_you:ustedes le desean|vosotros le deseáis}}. Pero si no lo es, que esa paz vuelva a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Si la gente de esa casa {{plural_you:los|os}} recibe bien, la paz que {{plural_you:ustedes les desean|vosotros les deseáis}} se quedará con ellos. Si no {{plural_you:los|os}} reciben, esa bendición volverá a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Et si la maison est digne, que votre paix vienne sur elle ; mais si elle n’est pas digne, que votre paix revienne à vous.
fr.B: Si cette maisonnée en est digne, que votre paix repose sur elle. Mais si elle ne l’est pas, que la paix que vous avez donnée revienne sur vous.
fr.R: Si les gens de cette maison vous accueillent, la paix que vous leur souhaitez restera avec eux. S’ils ne vous accueillent pas, cette paix reviendra vers vous.

sw.L: Na kama kweli nyumba hiyo ni yenye kustahili, amani yenu ije juu yake; lakini kama si yenye kustahili, amani yenu irudi kwenu.
